name: Pedal Stew
tagline: A pedal steel with a breakfast shift
bio: Used to practice behind a diner counter until the cook offered a permanent corner. Plays sweet high harmonies and refuses to end a tune before everyone gets a solo.
lookingFor: An upright bassist and a brush drummer for a three-song country shuffle set.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pedal Stew in a small club with diner-stool pedal steel.

name: Organ Darnell
tagline: The organ has one hot key
bio: One key on his organ throws a spark every time he lands a turnaround. He swears it only happens in B-flat and leaves the bench open for anyone who knows the bridge.
lookingFor: An alto singer and a drummer who can hold a slow pocket under four-part harmonies.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Organ Darnell in a small club with broken-key electric organ.

name: Banjo Signal
bio: Built a banjo that picks up the weather report between songs. Plays traditional rolls underneath melodies that sound like they came from a moon landing.
lookingFor: A fiddle player for fiddle-and-banjo duets in odd meters.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Banjo Signal in a small club with satellite-dish open-back banjo.

name: Busker Biscuit
bio: His harmonica spits out a bus ticket on every bent note. The collection is organized by route, key and whether the middle eight was any good.
lookingFor: A fingerstyle guitarist for stripped-down blues duos.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Busker Biscuit in a small club with ticket-punch harmonica set.

name: Fringe Dente
bio: The guitar strings are pasta, so she keeps a spare box backstage. Her songs are built for shout-along choruses and the first dance after the heartbreak song.
lookingFor: A bass player comfortable with fast two-steps and tight stops.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Fringe Dente in a small club with spaghetti-string electric guitar.

name: Roadcase Rae
bio: Learned to tune ratchets, handles and road-case wheels while loading bands in. Now she can set up a good-sounding kit in two minutes, including the squeaky kick pedal.
lookingFor: A bassist and a singer for a portable rehearsal setup.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Roadcase Rae in a small club with rolling flight-case kit.

name: Fiddle Fern
tagline: Water twice a week in D major
bio: His case grows a new fern frond every time he nails a double stop. He likes old dance tunes with long gaps to let the room breathe.
lookingFor: A clawhammer banjo player for quiet old-time sessions.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Fiddle Fern in a small club with fern-lined fiddle case.

name: Velvet Frequency
bio: Sings like a late-night radio host reading a love letter through a busted console. A neon heart hangs over the mic and dims when somebody sings flat.
lookingFor: A pedal steel player and a pianist for a harmony-heavy country soul trio.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Velvet Frequency in a small club with broadcast microphone.

name: Pickle Pocket
bio: Each jar is filled to a different pitch, and no one is allowed to eat tomorrow’s downbeat. Her sets move from kitchen-table songs to dancing without changing the tempo.
lookingFor: An acoustic guitarist and a second singer for bilingual folk harmonies.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pickle Pocket in a small club with pickle-jar shakers.

name: Mando Forecast
bio: Checks his mandolin’s weather vane before picking a key. Wants to record a batch of two-minute tunes that sound like summer storms rolling over the Cumberland.
lookingFor: A flatpicker who likes trading lead breaks and writing quick instrumentals.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Mando Forecast in a small club with weather-vane mandolin.

name: Ironing Chords
bio: Found the perfect stand in the laundry room, then spent a decade figuring out one four-note voicing. Hears the bass line before she hears the melody.
lookingFor: A bass player and drummer for a Rhodes-style soul trio.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Ironing Chords in a small club with ironing-board keyboard.

name: Motel Lowline
bio: Her bass doubles as the key to a room that doesn’t exist. She has a stack of wiry country-funk sketches and needs a band that knows when to stay on the one.
lookingFor: A drummer who likes short funky tunes and a guitarist who leaves space.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Motel Lowline in a small club with motel-fob bass.

name: Kick In A Case
bio: The suitcase kick is stuffed with unmatched socks, each with a different damping curve. He records full takes and keeps the chair noises if they land in rhythm.
lookingFor: A songwriter with a quiet voice who wants to record live takes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Kick In A Case in a small club with suitcase kick drum.

name: Dialtone Dottie
bio: Routes the lead synth through an old switchboard and answers wrong numbers in harmony. The best new songs started as voicemails she forgot to delete.
lookingFor: A guitarist and harmony singer for twangy synth-pop.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Dialtone Dottie in a small club with patch-cord synth.

name: Baritone Shortstack
tagline: A short stack and a long scale
bio: Writes riffs in the booth while the second pot of coffee brews. Plays low and dry, then adds one ridiculous turnaround just to see who is listening.
lookingFor: A drummer for slow desert grooves and a bass player who likes drop tunings.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Baritone Shortstack in a small club with baritone electric guitar.

name: Jukebox June Bug
bio: Took the guts out of a jukebox and learned to bow the shell. Collects songs with three chords and writes counter-melodies that turn up again in the outro.
lookingFor: A vocalist and acoustic guitarist for arrangements that leave space for cello.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Jukebox June Bug in a small club with jukebox-body cello.

name: Cone Solo Cal
tagline: Merge left at the vocal break
bio: Sings harmony so loudly the city issued him a spare traffic cone. He is happiest playing a B-side with a long organ solo rather than doing a set of hits.
lookingFor: A rhythm guitarist and keys player for loose country-soul sessions.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Cone Solo Cal in a small club with traffic-cone vocal mic.

name: The Tiny Pedal Choir
tagline: Eight tiny boxes and a tenor
bio: Builds tiny choirs with pedals and assigns each pedal its own part. Wants to bring in real voices, keep all the imperfections and make the chorus big enough to rattle the stage.
lookingFor: Two singers for harmony experiments and live vocal loops.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician The Tiny Pedal Choir in a small club with miniature vocal-loop pedals.

name: Lamp Shade Lynn
tagline: The shade goes on at showtime
bio: Her lampshade hat doubles as a lyric prompt. Each panel has a first line written inside, and the audience picks which panel she has to sing from.
lookingFor: A harmony singer who likes classic country storytelling and soft fingerpicking.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Lamp Shade Lynn in a small club with flat-top acoustic guitar.

name: Bubble Squeezebox
bio: Put a bubble valve on his bellows because dry rehearsals felt too serious. Writes fast dance tunes with clear endings that even a tired drummer can hear.
lookingFor: A washboard player and a fiddler for two-step dance tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Bubble Squeezebox in a small club with bubble-valve button accordion.

name: Taco Tremolo
bio: Keeps a breakfast taco plugged into the amp so the tremolo smells like eggs by the second chorus. Every verse has to fit inside two minutes.
lookingFor: An upright bassist and drummer for fast, sweaty rockabilly sets.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Taco Tremolo in a small club with breakfast-taco guitar.

name: Bicycle Bell Bea
bio: Built a tambourine from retired bike bells. She reminds everyone that a wrong note is only a wrong note if you don’t play it again in verse two.
lookingFor: A keyboard player and singer for short indie-pop songs.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Bicycle Bell Bea in a small club with bicycle-bell tambourine.

name: Register Ruckus
bio: The cash drawer is his kick and the receipt printer is his hi-hat. He keeps the register’s bell for transitions, because a chorus should earn that ding.
lookingFor: A bass player for a live beat set with quick changes and long grooves.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Register Ruckus in a small club with cash-register drum kit.

name: Prickly Fuzz
bio: Built a fuzz box that literally bites if stomped wrong. Tracks riffs before breakfast and votes against any pedal that needs more than two knobs.
lookingFor: A bassist and drummer who like low-volume psych jams and big endings.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Prickly Fuzz in a small club with cactus-spike fuzz pedal.

name: Brisket Belter
bio: The barbecue fork is a stage mic with a handle long enough to point at soloists. She saves her highest note for the point where the guitarist finally turns down.
lookingFor: A pianist and drummer for slow blues, soul shuffles and big harmonies.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Brisket Belter in a small club with barbecue-fork mic.

name: Meter Maid MIDI
bio: She bought an obsolete meter and replaced its guts with an eight-track sampler. When it flashes expired the group has to improvise a new bass line.
lookingFor: A bassist or horn player for live house jams around 120 BPM.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Meter Maid MIDI in a small club with parking-meter sampler.

name: Sax Fan Shai
tagline: The horn has three fan speeds
bio: The cooling fan was supposed to stop the horn fogging up, but she realized it made a good vibrato. Her ideal rehearsal has a groove you can hear from the sidewalk.
lookingFor: A keyboardist and drummer for a funk trio with rotating solos.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Sax Fan Shai in a small club with fan-cooled tenor sax.

name: Armadillo Arlo
bio: The shell lets him carry the bass on his back when the bus fills up. He can play a straight eighth-note part for an hour and make every fourth bar feel different.
lookingFor: A drummer and guitarist for weird garage tunes with clean stops.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Armadillo Arlo in a small club with armadillo-shell bass.

name: Batwing Bento
bio: His tremolo has two rubber wings that make it sound faster than it is. Writes short instrumental songs named after things found under the bridge.
lookingFor: A drummer and bass player for noisy instrumental surf rock.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Batwing Bento in a small club with bat-wing tremolo.

name: Fridge Magnet Fray
bio: Arranges the lyrics on a fridge and lets the magnets decide the order. It makes for crooked verses and remarkably tidy harmonies.
lookingFor: A synth player and drummer for jagged pop songs with weird hooks.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Fridge Magnet Fray in a small club with fridge-magnet mic.

name: Porch Swing Keys
bio: Converted a porch swing into a keyboard stand, then found the squeak matched the kick. Likes big group choruses and songs that can survive a key change.
lookingFor: A drummer and harmony singer for relaxed gospel-soul afternoons.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Porch Swing Keys in a small club with porch-swing keyboard.

name: Chile Chord Chuy
bio: Painted every tuning knob like a different pepper so he could tune by color in the dark. Wants to work up a little suite about the best late-night snacks in town.
lookingFor: A button accordion player and bassist for conjunto dance tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Chile Chord Chuy in a small club with chili-knob bajo sexto.

name: Pie Tin Pru
bio: Built a snare from the loudest pie tin at a family cookout. She plays quieter than anybody in the room and still somehow sets the pace.
lookingFor: An acoustic bassist and guitarist for low-volume swing sessions.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pie Tin Pru in a small club with pie-tin snare.

name: Longhorn LFO
bio: Bolted oversized horns onto the filter cutoff, which was great until the keyboard case stopped closing. He has forty patches and wants to write songs for three of them.
lookingFor: A drum machine nerd and a vocalist for an electro duo that can play live.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Longhorn LFO in a small club with longhorn-knob synthesizer.

name: Pump Organ Pip
bio: The pump dial charges by the slap, so she spends the first verse walking quarters. Keeps song forms simple and memorizes the singers’ cues.
lookingFor: A singer and a small-kit drummer for roadhouse-style rockabilly.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pump Organ Pip in a small club with gas-pump upright bass.

name: Cooler Beats Cole
bio: Cools his equipment with imaginary ice and writes the track list on the lid. Has enough unfinished beats for three records and wants to finish five with other players.
lookingFor: A rapper or bassist for short tape sets and live beat swaps.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Cooler Beats Cole in a small club with ice-chest sampler.

name: Umbrella Clarinet
bio: The bell opens if it rains, making a little roof over the reed. Her favorite musicians can play softly enough for someone to order a coffee mid-song.
lookingFor: A guitarist and upright bass player for patio clarinet sets.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Umbrella Clarinet in a small club with umbrella-bell clarinet.

name: Staple Gun Sami
tagline: Fasten the verse to the chorus
bio: Staples the chord charts to the wall by key. The capo looks like the office stapler, which is why he keeps losing it to the print shop downstairs.
lookingFor: A bassist and drummer who like tight eighth notes and sharp transitions.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Staple Gun Sami in a small club with staple-shaped capo.

name: Thunder Mic Taz
tagline: Rain delay in the middle eight
bio: Keeps a small storm inside the microphone grille. She tries new parts by whispering them first, then lets the drums decide which parts deserve thunder.
lookingFor: A keyboardist and drummer who enjoy shifting between spoken and sung lines.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Thunder Mic Taz in a small club with storm-globe vocal mic.

name: Icehouse Inez
bio: The bow squeaks whenever the ice compartment opens. She uses the sound as an accidental cue for every fade and keeps the recording if it happens twice.
lookingFor: A nylon-string guitarist and vocalist for spare, spacious arrangements.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Icehouse Inez in a small club with roadside-ice-machine cello.

name: Star Mirror Sabine
tagline: A vanity mirror with an oscillator
bio: Bought a vanity mirror at a prop sale and wired its bulbs to the synth envelope. The nicest chords light up one corner at a time.
lookingFor: A bassist and a quiet drummer for late-night synth soul sets.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Star Mirror Sabine in a small club with star-mirror synthesizer.

name: Red Light Riff
bio: His amp changes the signal depending on how hard he strums. He likes riffs that can hold up through a whole intersection without a solo.
lookingFor: A drummer and bassist for short Latin garage songs with split-second breaks.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Red Light Riff in a small club with traffic-signal amp.

name: Hubcap Harvey
bio: Bought a drum kit one hubcap at a time. Each one has a different ding, and he keeps the shallowest for parts that need room under the vocals.
lookingFor: A bass player and singer for a grimy live-room rock recording.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Hubcap Harvey in a small club with chrome hubcap drums.

name: Bendy Straw Bex
bio: The talkbox hose rotates with every vowel, so she has perfected breath control while untangling it. Her songs should feel like machines telling a joke they barely understand.
lookingFor: A guitarist or bassist who wants to write danceable talkbox songs.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Bendy Straw Bex in a small club with bendy-straw talkbox.

name: Palm Tenor Pax
bio: A palm frond on the bell gives him a visible cue when he starts playing too loud. Wants a group that can vamp until everybody has found something interesting to say.
lookingFor: A keys player for a groove trio with room for horn solos.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Palm Tenor Pax in a small club with palm-tree tenor sax.

name: Gaffer Bass Gia
bio: Fixed the bass with different tape for every section of the song. Her favorite parts are one note played at exactly the right moment.
lookingFor: A drummer and rhythm guitarist for clipped, punchy post-punk.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Gaffer Bass Gia in a small club with gaffer-taped bass.

name: Foam Crooner Cruz
bio: Took a foam mic from a set because the weight felt right. Belts straight to the back wall anyway, then rewrites the bridge on the bus home.
lookingFor: A pianist and guitarist who like lounge covers turned sideways.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Foam Crooner Cruz in a small club with foam movie-prop mic.

name: Clapperboard Cal
bio: Slips a tiny clapperboard onto his finger as a slide. Musicians think he is asking them to start over when he is actually trying to play the sixth.
lookingFor: An acoustic guitarist for instrumental swing and lap steel tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Clapperboard Cal in a small club with clapperboard lap steel.

name: Pigeon Pads Paloma
bio: Two plastic pigeons peck the sampler buttons in remarkable time. She makes hazy drum loops and wants to give another player room to hijack one.
lookingFor: A spoken-word artist or sax player to trade ideas over dusty beats.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pigeon Pads Paloma in a small club with toy-pigeon sampler.

name: Ticket Stack Tilda
bio: Sheets of tickets cushion the keys she used to hit too hard. She rehearses in fifteen-minute bursts and treats a two-note hook like a civic duty.
lookingFor: A guitarist and bassist for fast songs that fit inside a parking meter.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Ticket Stack Tilda in a small club with parking-ticket keyboard.

name: Fishbowl Fable
bio: Uses the empty fishbowl as a head-sized echo chamber. Her songs start with an overheard sentence and end in a high harmony no one saw coming.
lookingFor: A keys player for strange pop songs with unusual harmonies.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Fishbowl Fable in a small club with fishbowl vocal helmet.

name: Saucer Scratcher
bio: Both decks look like they could leave the room at an irresponsible speed. He builds routines where the quietest scratch marks the biggest transition.
lookingFor: A percussionist or MC for short sets built around live cuts.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Saucer Scratcher in a small club with flying-saucer turntables.

name: Takeout Treble
bio: Stacks takeout boxes to measure the length of a rehearsal. She writes string parts that pull against the drums and loves when a crooked phrase turns catchy.
lookingFor: A percussionist and guitarist for short arrangements in uneven meters.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Takeout Treble in a small club with violin.

name: Gas Pedal Gospel
bio: Rewired the organ bass pedals using parts from a car that never ran. He can hold a verse together with his left foot while someone else learns the form.
lookingFor: A vocalist and drummer for organ trio jams.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Gas Pedal Gospel in a small club with car-pedal organ.

name: Freeway Firmware
tagline: No lane changes after bar eight
bio: The roads on her drum machine show traffic flow for every pattern. Nothing sounds quite right until at least one lane is backed up.
lookingFor: A horn player or bassist for live dance tracks with jagged drums.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Freeway Firmware in a small club with freeway drum machine.

name: Patch Cable Pete
bio: Wove a guitar out of a drawerful of faulty cables. His riffs are slow and heavy, but he takes notes in a neat little ruled notebook.
lookingFor: A drummer for riff rehearsals and a bassist who enjoys tuning low.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Patch Cable Pete in a small club with patch-cable baritone guitar.

name: Red Carpet Rita
bio: The case opens like a tiny awards ceremony, even in a laundromat. She plays old dance songs with new verses about everybody’s commute.
lookingFor: A hand percussionist for bilingual accordion-and-vocal sets.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Red Carpet Rita in a small club with red-carpet accordion.

name: Whistle Stop Wren
bio: She glued a whistle to the bell to mark the skanks without shouting. Can make a four-note melody sound good on the first pass with strangers.
lookingFor: A trombonist and drummer for bouncy porch-volume brass tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Whistle Stop Wren in a small club with traffic-whistle trumpet.

name: Camera Case Crash
tagline: Four cases and a good racket
bio: Builds her kit from film equipment cases left over from shoots. The kick takes a surprising amount of tuning, but the carrying handles are unbeatable.
lookingFor: A bassist and songwriter for three-minute guitar-pop songs.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Camera Case Crash in a small club with film-case drum kit.

name: Moon Peg Marcus
bio: The moon-shaped tuning peg is too large to leave in the case. His playing is patient and quiet, with slightly dramatic bowed notes at the end of a phrase.
lookingFor: A pianist or horn player for spacious jazz arrangements.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Moon Peg Marcus in a small club with moon-peg upright bass.

name: Turnstile Tenor
bio: The horn clicks once every time he plays a major seventh. He calls the noise a feature and asks for the melody at least twice before anyone solos.
lookingFor: A pianist and bassist to trade heads on fast bebop tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Turnstile Tenor in a small club with turnstile tenor sax.

name: Pizza Peel Pia
tagline: Serve the chorus by the slice
bio: The mic is long enough to pass over the front row. She changes the middle of a song every week, trusting the group to remember the hook.
lookingFor: A synth player and drummer for fast songs with dance beats.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pizza Peel Pia in a small club with pizza-peel microphone.

name: Till Beat Theo
tagline: Receipt says the snare is free
bio: The bodega drawer locks on the first beat so the rest of the pattern can move around. He keeps a notebook full of samples he could swear he heard in a stairwell.
lookingFor: An MC or bassist for sketching beats into three-minute songs.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Till Beat Theo in a small club with bodega till drum machine.

name: Crane Bow Kit
bio: The skyline crane bow can only just fit through the practice-room door. They prefer small melodies played slowly enough to hear the room change around them.
lookingFor: A guitarist or percussionist to collaborate on quiet instrumentals.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Crane Bow Kit in a small club with crane-arm violin bow.

name: Folding Keys Frankie
bio: Can fold her entire piano into a square that fits under the kitchen table. Plays the first verse with two fingers, then shows exactly why she held back.
lookingFor: A vocalist and upright bassist for jazz standards rearranged as soul tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Folding Keys Frankie in a small club with folding-chair grand piano.

name: Bagel Bell Bess
bio: The bagel got stuck during soundcheck and now she claims it improves her low notes. Plays dance tunes slowly for new players, then sees how far they can push the tempo.
lookingFor: An accordionist and upright bassist for klezmer and swing transitions.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Bagel Bell Bess in a small club with bagel-bell clarinet.

name: Radiator Rai
tagline: Heat comes on in the bridge
bio: His bass makes a little knock as it warms up. He sets the rehearsal heater to the same key and writes long verses for bands that want room to move.
lookingFor: A drummer and guitarist for angular songs and long instrumental intros.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Radiator Rai in a small club with radiator bass.

name: Hydrant Hands Hana
bio: Painted the congas red to keep strangers from taking them home after sessions. Reads percussion charts fast and will happily show a newcomer the bell pattern.
lookingFor: A pianist and bassist for small-group salsa arrangements.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Hydrant Hands Hana in a small club with fire-hydrant congas.

name: Disco Ballad Dot
bio: The mic throws light around the room when their voice hits a long note. They have a ballad collection and want to see which songs can survive a four-on-the-floor beat.
lookingFor: A bassist and keyboardist for theatrical dance ballads.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Disco Ballad Dot in a small club with spiked disco-ball mic.

name: Receipt Synth Ren
tagline: Take a number for the solo
bio: The synth prints a ticket every time she saves a patch. Her bandmates are allowed to pull a number and demand that sound on the next song.
lookingFor: A singer and drum programmer for clever, minimal synth-pop.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Receipt Synth Ren in a small club with deli-ticket synth.

name: Subway Slide Sol
tagline: Stand clear of the closing slide
bio: The slide makes a satisfying clunk between positions. He stopped trying to hide it and now builds his best riffs around the door sound.
lookingFor: A trumpet player and a drummer for street-volume brass arrangements.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Subway Slide Sol in a small club with subway-door trombone.

name: Quarter Drop Quinn
bio: Uses quarters as counters for loop lengths and always runs out in the final song. They like drums that build slowly enough for dancers to surprise themselves.
lookingFor: A bassist or percussionist to build live house sets with long transitions.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Quarter Drop Quinn in a small club with laundry-quarter dj mixer.

name: Broken Brolly Noor
tagline: The bow folds on the rest
bio: Replaced a broken bow with an umbrella rib and decided it sounded better. She writes long notes underneath short verses and keeps the takes where the room is audible.
lookingFor: A fingerstyle guitarist and singer for two-part acoustic arrangements.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Broken Brolly Noor in a small club with umbrella-bow cello.

name: Takeout Tom-Tom
tagline: Comes with a side of hi-hat
bio: Rates cup lids by how long they ring after a rimshot. He can build a convincing beat from your takeout order and still leave enough space for a bass line.
lookingFor: A bassist for dry funk grooves with plenty of space for the drums.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Takeout Tom-Tom in a small club with takeout-cup percussion.

name: Taxi Meter Max
bio: The pickup counts down every time someone says one more take. She keeps riffs short and votes to stop a rehearsal while everyone is still excited.
lookingFor: A drummer and bassist for fast, abrasive two-minute songs.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Taxi Meter Max in a small club with taxi-meter guitar pickup.

name: Moving Box Min
bio: His keyboard has been packed for an imaginary move for three years. Pulls ideas from whatever old set lists he ends up using for box padding.
lookingFor: A drummer and singer for new songs that start from chord loops.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Moving Box Min in a small club with moving-box keyboard stand.

name: Fire Escape Eve
tagline: Take the stairs to the high note
bio: The mic cable runs up a miniature fire escape before reaching the PA. She writes songs with a good first line and rehearses the last harmony until it sticks.
lookingFor: A drummer and bassist for vocal-forward guitar music with strange bridges.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Fire Escape Eve in a small club with fire-escape patch-cable mic.

name: Stoop Scoop Luz
bio: The instrument has three small steps carved into the body. She uses each step for a slightly different thumb attack and refuses to put extra fills under a good lyric.
lookingFor: A percussionist and guitar player for slow summer soul tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Stoop Scoop Luz in a small club with brownstone-stoop bass.

name: Platform Brush Benny
bio: Built two brushes from miniature station brooms. He sweeps the snare in broad circles and keeps an index card of songs everybody knows in a different key.
lookingFor: An upright bassist and acoustic guitarist for swing at conversation volume.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Platform Brush Benny in a small club with subway-broom brushes.

name: Elevator Reed Arun
bio: The harmonium bellows rise and fall like an ancient elevator. Their songs start low and bring in more people one phrase at a time.
lookingFor: A hand drummer and a chorus singer for long, patient modal jams.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Elevator Reed Arun in a small club with elevator harmonium.

name: Lightning Lick Leon
bio: Bolted a little lightning rod to the guitar after a surprise outdoor storm. He’d rather hear a groove develop than run through a dozen songs nobody remembers.
lookingFor: A bassist and harp player for slow Chicago blues and loud turnarounds.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Lightning Lick Leon in a small club with lightning-rod electric guitar.

name: Deep Dish Di
tagline: Extra cheese on the high note
bio: Sawed a pizza cutter into a microphone stand and never took it off. She writes sharp little songs about chores, then sings the last line like it matters more than anything.
lookingFor: A guitarist and drummer for crunchy pop songs and harmonized bridges.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Deep Dish Di in a small club with pizza-cutter microphone.

name: Snow Day Sequencer
bio: The drum machine freezes on a pattern if you stop turning the knobs. He keeps the groove steady enough for dancers while changing everything underneath it.
lookingFor: A bassist or singer for long house jams with live drums.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Snow Day Sequencer in a small club with snowflake drum machine.

name: Wind Chime Wil
tagline: The bell keeps its own time
bio: The end of his horn is a wind chime that rings after he stops a phrase. He uses long rests until everybody hears where the tune wants to go next.
lookingFor: A percussionist and pianist to write horn hooks for funk and Latin jazz.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Wind Chime Wil in a small club with wind-chime baritone sax.

name: Drawbridge Dee
tagline: Raise the bridge at the bridge
bio: A toy drawbridge lifts from the bass neck whenever she hits its switch. She wraps jagged rhythms around a strong downbeat and likes to leave the difficult part until the end.
lookingFor: A guitarist and drummer to write three angular instrumentals.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Drawbridge Dee in a small club with drawbridge bass.

name: Radiator Rhodes Rox
tagline: Heat up the low notes first
bio: Set her piano on a cast-iron radiator that ticks in the rests. She uses the sound as a pulse and isn’t afraid to let a one-chord intro go on until everyone settles in.
lookingFor: A singer and drummer for gospel-flavored jazz songs.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Radiator Rhodes Rox in a small club with radiator-stand electric piano.

name: Windup Willa
bio: Her shaker runs for exactly four minutes before it needs to be wound again. She paces a set by the ratchet and always gives the bass player room to answer.
lookingFor: A bassist and accordionist for dance tunes built around the percussion.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Windup Willa in a small club with wind-up meter percussion.

name: Gate Arm Gary
tagline: Wait for the noise to pass
bio: The pickup works fine until he drops the crossing gate on the strings. He gives a riff three tries, then cuts it in half and plays that part twice.
lookingFor: A drummer to build tense instrumental songs with sudden quiet sections.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Gate Arm Gary in a small club with train gate tremolo arm.

name: Electric Mitten Mox
tagline: Gloved hand on the lead break
bio: The trumpet stays warm because the mitten plugs into its bell. They play small musical arguments with the drummer and leave the reply hanging for a chorus.
lookingFor: A trombonist and percussionist for a compact street brass group.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Electric Mitten Mox in a small club with electric-mitten trumpet.

name: Relish Vibes Val
bio: Swapped the vibraphone bars for glowing green ones after losing the third octave in a dim club. She likes melodies that can be played as a question or an answer.
lookingFor: An upright bassist and guitarist for quiet jazz with unusual melodies.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Relish Vibes Val in a small club with relish-green vibraphone.

name: Buoy Bang Beto
tagline: Channel marker in a mosh pit
bio: The buckets have enough ring to hear across the lake. He gets the group through a full set in rehearsal and still leaves time to argue about the last song.
lookingFor: A bassist and singer for loud songs that end on time.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Buoy Bang Beto in a small club with lake-buoy bucket drums.

name: Spark Plug Slip
bio: The harmonica rattles like an engine that’s almost ready to turn over. His best parts are little two-bar answers to lyrics about people who missed their train.
lookingFor: A guitarist and drummer for electric blues and country shuffles.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Spark Plug Slip in a small club with sparkplug harmonica.

name: Dibs Desk Drea
bio: Keeps a tiny folding chair on top of the sampler so other producers know which desk is hers. Loves taking a catchy one-bar melody through an unreasonable number of drum patterns.
lookingFor: A vocalist or percussionist for warm house songs with short hooks.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Dibs Desk Drea in a small club with parking-chair sampler.

name: Derby Doorstop
bio: Broke three pedals by stomping, then solved it with a chunk of rubber from a door. Wears derby pads because the rehearsal rug keeps sliding across the floor.
lookingFor: A bassist and drummer for loud rehearsals and short sets.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Derby Doorstop in a small club with doorstop distortion pedal.

name: Lamppost Lulu
bio: The lamp buzzes when the mic is on, which made the opening note easy to find. They sing the last verse for whoever had to wait for the bus in the rain.
lookingFor: A bassist and pianist to arrange quiet verses and big dance choruses.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Lamppost Lulu in a small club with street-lamp mic.

name: Pothole Pizz Piper
tagline: Mind the gap under the endpin
bio: The cello endpin fits perfectly in a piece of broken road. She drags a bow across two strings for a whole verse, then answers with a spare pizzicato line.
lookingFor: A drummer and guitarist for instrumental sketches that build slowly.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Pothole Pizz Piper in a small club with pothole-pin cello.

name: Plow Tempo Parth
bio: Stuck a toy plow on his bigger drum and insists it clears away beats that aren’t working. He writes concise rhythm charts and leaves room for somebody to ignore them.
lookingFor: A keyboardist or bassist for modal jams with shifting meters.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Plow Tempo Parth in a small club with snowplow tabla.

name: Coil String Coral
bio: Replaced two strings with silver springs and now has to catch the notes before they bounce away. Plays big quiet phrases and thinks the best solos usually end early.
lookingFor: A reed player and drummer for improvised music with a clear pulse.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Coil String Coral in a small club with spring-strung upright bass.

name: Lunch Counter Lou
bio: The pedal steel table looks like a two-seat lunch counter, complete with a napkin holder. Lou keeps a small book of songs that deserve a steel part and brings extra charts.
lookingFor: A vocalist and upright bassist for lap-and-pedal-steel swing tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Lunch Counter Lou in a small club with lunch-counter pedal steel.

name: Life Raft Lark
tagline: Carry a spare for the bridge
bio: A tiny life raft dangles from the trumpet bell so she can point it at whoever is rushing. Knows exactly how far a quiet horn can carry in a small room.
lookingFor: A percussionist and trombonist to rehearse neighborhood brass tunes.
portraitAlt: Fictional musician Life Raft Lark in a small club with life-raft trumpet.
